notes: POWO and Flora of North America recognize Euphorbia davidii as accepted.
This species was historically entangled with Euphorbia dentata var. cuphosperma / E. cuphosperma concepts.

target_zone_range_leads.guardrail: Range evidence is conflicting. Deep Review must resolve Texas nativity carefully and should not force a PASS/FAIL from this Scout draft.
leads: Master Plant Pool has 1 personal wild observation.
POWO currently lists Texas as introduced.
FNA includes Texas and describes E. davidii as native from the southwestern United States and northern Mexico through the southern Great Plains, adventive elsewhere.
Montana Field Guide notes that some database treatments have historically misinterpreted E. davidii's native status.
BONAP county maps should be checked, but county presence alone does not resolve native versus introduced status.

morphology_candidate.look_here_first: Separate it from E. dentata using texture and seed/fruit, not casual habit. E. davidii tends to have shorter, stiffer hairs with tiny pustular bases, larger capsules and seeds, often more elliptic leaves, and angular irregularly lumpy seeds.
diagnostic_traits: mostly opposite leaves with irregular coarse teeth
leaf undersides with relatively stout short hairs, often on minute pustular bases
capsules broadly ovoid and generally larger than E. dentata
seeds larger, angular in cross section, irregularly low-tuberculate or wrinkled

confusers.separator: E. davidii generally has larger fruit/seeds, more elliptic leaves, shorter stiffer pustule-based hairs, and angular irregular seeds; E. dentata has smaller, more uniformly ovoid finely pebbled seeds and longer/less-stiff hairs.
